notes: CACHE-BACKED TAR-LAYER E2E, DEMONSTRATED ON MACOS FOR THIS CONTROLLED RUN. Three genuinely different versions of the example app were built by cargo tauri build; their main binaries hash to dd42cb31..., 573f3838... and 7caff690... (SHA-256), asserted pairwise distinct by both the build script and the runner so no downstream assertion can pass vacuously. TRANSITION 1: real v1.0.0 with an EMPTY cache, advertised v1.0.1, selected FULL -- which is the required outcome, because no valid base exists and no direct base artifact was supplied. The exact official v1.0.1 artifact was downloaded, hash- and signature-verified, staged as PENDING, and installed through the real tauri_plugin_updater Update::install. The installed main binary hashed to 573f3838..., exactly v1.0.1. The app was then relaunched, reported version 1.0.1 about itself, and the cache promoted PENDING -> ACTIVE. TRANSITION 2: real v1.0.1 with ACTIVE(1.0.1), advertised v1.0.2 with a generated tar-layer patch, selected TARDELTA. Only 633594 bytes were downloaded against a 4167008-byte artifact (15.205%). The server's request log confirms the tar patch was fetched and that neither the full artifact nor the direct patch was -- so the saving is observed at the wire, not inferred from a reported number. The cached artifact was re-verified, expanded to the exact old tar, patched, recompressed in-process to the exact official .app.tar.gz, digest- and signature-verified, staged as PENDING and installed through the real Update::install. The installed main binary hashed to 7caff690..., exactly v1.0.2. Relaunch reported 1.0.2 and promoted ACTIVE. CHAIN EVIDENCE: the base_tar_blake3 of the 1.0.1->1.0.2 tar patch (804d769f3cfb1ca883f417351e0fff6ed2329dd313aa635ef252de38fe9f0a0c) is identical to the target_tar_blake3 of the 1.0.0->1.0.1 release, so the artifact transition 2 patched against is provably the one transition 1 cached. BANDWIDTH: direct compressed-artifact patches were 95.1986% and 96.5456% of a full download; tar-layer patches for the same pairs were 15.0361% and 15.205%, i.e. 84.2056% and 84.2509% fewer patch bytes. This reproduces the earlier controlled single-pair result (15.36% vs 95.43%) on two independent pairs from a fresh build. RECOMPRESSION ON FRESH ARTIFACTS: delta-release round-tripped both releases before publishing -- it applied its own patch, recompressed, and required byte-identity with the artifact cargo tauri build had just produced. That is independent of the committed fixture: it shows the recipe reproduces artifacts from the current toolchain, not only one retained from August. DEGRADATION: with the cached blob corrupted at one byte (same length), a real run selected FULL, downloaded the full artifact, and still installed v1.0.2 correctly. SCOPE, EXACTLY. macOS only, one architecture, one bundle format, one three-version ladder, string-only source changes between versions, plain-HTTP loopback enabled through the e2e-control feature, ad-hoc code signing. It demonstrates integration and the cache state machine under a real installer; it is not a general macOS claim, not a performance claim, and closes no Audit #2 blocker. The transition timings (0.113 s and 0.276 s) are control-surface round trips over loopback with no network latency and are not a benchmark. Decompression and recompression were not timed separately.
artifact_provenance: Built by examples/desktop-app/e2e/build-three-versions.sh, which runs `cargo tauri build --features e2e-control` three times against examples/desktop-app with only the version string changed, then publishes both releases with the delta-release binary built from this tree at --require-tar-layer. No manifest field is written by the harness: the runner rewrites only URLs, because the port is ephemeral. The signing key is generated per run into the output directory and never committed. Artifacts, manifests, patches and e2e-report.json are retained under /private/tmp/delta-tar-e2e. Re-runnable from the repository with build-three-versions.sh followed by run-tar-e2e.sh on macOS arm64 with cargo-tauri 2.10.1 installed.
